variations: Chalk snail trail: draw a spiral on paving with non-toxic sidewalk chalk, put your dog's sniff dots along it and rinse it away afterwards. Skip the chalk if your dog licks the sidewalk.
Seated version: use a smaller 2 by 2 meter spiral on a rug and sit at the edge throughout.
Tiny version: one loop of tape around a mat, with three dots.
Puppy or senior version: wider lanes, fewer dots, and a thicker rest mat at the center.
supplies: Low-tack painter's tape or flat rope
A little of today's regular food
optionalSupplies: Paper and a pencil for the plan
A phone for the overhead photo
substitutes: No tape? Use a line of rolled towels laid flat or a clothesline rope pegged flat on grass.
title: The Hallway Labyrinth
clue: A floor pattern with no wrong turns and a quiet place at the very middle.
reveal: Lay a life-size spiral on the floor or the lawn, scatter a few sniff dots along it, and let your dog wander in. The walls are only suggestions, and the center is a place to rest, not a finish line.
objective: Build a small spiral labyrinth, let your dog explore it at their own pace, and end with a rest at the center.
instructions: Sketch a spiral on paper first if it helps. Then lay it out about 3 by 3 meters with low-tack painter's tape on the floor, or flat rope on the lawn, leaving the lanes at least two dog-widths wide. Test the tape on a hidden spot first.
Put a non-slip rug under any slippery floor, and place a mat or folded blanket in the middle as the center.
Lay six to eight pieces of today's ration along the path as sniff dots, spaced irregularly. Put a slightly better-smelling piece on the center mat.
Invite your dog in. Walk the path beside them on a loose leash outdoors, or sit and watch if you are indoors. They set the pace, and stepping over the lines counts as a valid route.
At the center, sit and be still. Offer water. The center is for rest, so let them lie down, sniff, or leave.
Take your overhead photo from a chair before anything is moved. When your dog has moved off, peel the tape up in a slow reel, so the labyrinth 'melts' away.
twist: The walls are optional, so there is no wrong way through. Dogs never fail a labyrinth.
completion: Your dog has explored the labyrinth, over or through the lines, or you have enjoyed the build and the center mat with them.
photoIdea: A tall overhead photo of the labyrinth with your dog resting on the center mat, taken from a chair.
memoryPrompt: What route did your dog take, and what did the center turn into?
dietNotes: Use part of today's normal ration and count it in. Ask your vet if your dog has dietary restrictions, allergies or health conditions.
safety: Lay low-tack tape or rope flat on a non-slip floor, never as a loose leash, and take it up afterwards.
Skip tape and rope for dogs who mouth floor items; use rolled towels instead.
Use only part of today's normal food, never chocolate, grapes, raisins or xylitol.
